docs.title: Irreducible Trade-offs
docs.text:
Choice Gain Loss On-device AI Privacy, offline latency Model quality, update velocity, device cost Federated learning Privacy, scale Convergence speed, debugging difficulty BT mesh Offline safety Battery, complexity, security surface OSM base layer Cost, openness Freshness, completeness Community data Coverage, cost Trust, validation load Cross-platform Reach Performance parity, native feature access Temporal layers Rich context Storage explosion, query complexity

Key Decision: Privacy over model quality; offline over fresh. Correct strategic bet, requires architectural compensation.

docs.title: ADR-0001: Documentation-First Authoring
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-09-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The AI-Smart-Maps blueprint requires Rust, ONNX, BLE mesh, federated learning, and edge infrastructure. No-code tooling cannot build that. But the blueprint itself is unstructured, contains encoding corruption, and lacks API contracts, schemas, and phase-gate criteria.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Author all architectural documentation in Markdown + Git + MkDocs Material. Treat the blueprint as source material, not as an implementation target. No-code applies to documentation authoring only.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Fast iteration on structured docs
  • Validation via schemas and pytest
  • Product implementation remains a separate, code-first track

docs.title: ADR-0002: Decentralized Tile Federation (DTF)
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The blueprint implies a centralized tile/graph server. Outage, DDoS, or censorship causes global failure.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt content-addressed tiles with peer discovery. Any node can serve any tile. Signed tiles prevent tampering. No central authority required for reads.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Removes single point of failure
  • Censorship-resistant
  • Requires signing infrastructure and peer discovery protocol
  • Adds complexity to tile versioning

docs.title: ADR-0003: Multi-Tier Federated Learning with Byzantine Resistance (MTFL-BR)
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Naive federated learning is vulnerable to model poisoning. No convergence guarantees. Debugging is near-impossible.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Four tiers: device updates (DP noise), regional aggregation (Krum / trimmed mean), global synthesis (golden dataset validation), canary deployment (1% rollout with auto-rollback).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Byzantine resistance at regional tier
  • Full model lineage for audit
  • Slower convergence than naive FL
  • Requires golden dataset maintenance

docs.title: ADR-0004: Zero-Trust Mesh Architecture (ZTMA)
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: BT mesh is vulnerable to Sybil, eclipse, replay, jamming, wormhole, and identity spoofing attacks.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Layered mitigations: proof-of-work for participation, multi-path routing, monotonic sequence numbers with 50ms timestamp window, BLE 5.4 channel hopping, physical plausibility checks, ephemeral keys rotating every 15 minutes.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Robust against known mesh attacks
  • Higher battery and CPU cost
  • Requires hardware support for BLE 5.4 channel selection

docs.title: ADR-0005: Format-Agnostic Routing Abstraction Layer (FARAL)
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Routing tied to a specific map format locks in vendor and data source.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Define a Unified Spatial Graph Interface (nodes, edges, weights, constraints, temporal). Adapters for OSM, commercial, custom, and real-time data. Routing algorithms operate on the interface, not the format.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• New data sources require new adapter, not new engine
  • Small abstraction overhead per query
  • Requires strict interface versioning

docs.title: ADR-0006: Temporal Data Lifecycle Architecture (TDLA)
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Temporal layers with no retention policy cause unbounded storage growth and query degradation.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Four tiers: HOT (0–7 days, in-memory), WARM (7–90 days, SSD), COLD (90 days–2 years, object storage), ARCHIVE (>2 years, compressed). Deletion policy: user data within 30 days on request; community reports anonymized after 90 days; mesh messages never persisted.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Bounded storage growth
  • Predictable query latency per tier
  • Requires tier-migration automation

docs.title: ADR-0007: Confidence-Aware Offline Mode (CAOM)
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-24

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Offline AI quality drops silently. Users do not know they are receiving degraded routes. Safety risk.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Every route and decision carries a confidence score derived from map data age, community report density, model version, route novelty, and environmental complexity. Below 60% confidence, warn the user and prefer known-safe roads.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Transparency for degraded operation
  • Requires confidence calibration per model version
  • May reduce perceived performance when honest

docs.title: Phase Gates
docs.text: Each phase requires explicit go/no-go review by the Architecture Review Board.

docs.title: Gate Criteria
docs.text: Phase Must Pass Before Advancing P0 Foundation Blueprint reviewed; docs scaffold builds; validator passes P1 Core Routing engine alpha with 1K users; latency budgets met P2 AI On-device inference <5% quality delta; canary pipeline live P3 Mesh <100ms hazard propagation in pilot zone; battery <3%/day P4 Scale 1M users, 10 cities; edge caches stable under 10M req/s peak P5 Evolve Global deployment; independent security audit passed

docs.title: Conditional Advance
docs.text: A phase may advance conditionally if: - All critical risks have mitigations in place - No unresolved existential assumption (A1, A2, A4, A9) - Architecture Review Board records the exception

docs.title: Six Irreducible Mandates
docs.text: ID Objective Architectural Mandate Success Metric O1 AI-powered smart shortcuts Real-time graph optimization with multi-objective cost functions Route quality > Google/Waze in blind A/B tests O2 Privacy-first design Zero-knowledge architecture; no PII at rest or in transit Zero data-breach blast radius O3 Cross-platform delivery Single logical system, multiple render targets Feature parity within 2 weeks of release O4 Offline-full AI On-device inference parity with cloud <5% quality delta offline vs online O5 Community-powered data Byzantine-fault-tolerant contribution pipeline >95% report accuracy at scale O6 Bluetooth mesh safety Sub-100ms peer-to-peer hazard propagation 30% accident reduction in pilot zones

docs.title: Tension Web
docs.text:
Mandates are not independent:

  • O2 (privacy) constrains O5 (community data)
  • O4 (offline) limits AI model size, constraining O1 (shortcut quality)
  • O6 (mesh latency) forces edge-first processing with zero cloud dependency

This tension is the central architectural challenge.
